summary.en: Afghan Taliban forces opened fire on Pakistani security forces along the Kurram border, prompting an intelligence-led army response that killed a Pakistani officer and several terrorists in Balochistan. Pakistan suspended trade at two Iran border crossings, citing security and smuggling concerns, while trade with Afghanistan fell sharply after border closures. Pakistan also announced plans to open a consulate in Benghazi, Libya, and the navy outlined a new strategy pairing mesh networking with long-range strike capability. 1,794 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Afghanske Taliban-styrker åpnet ild mot pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker langs Kurram-grensen, noe som førte til et etterretningsledet hærrespons som drepte en pakistansk offiser og flere terrorister i Balochistan. Pakistan suspendert handel ved to grenseoverganger til Iran, med begrunnelse i sikkerhets- og smuglingsbekymringer, mens handelen med Afghanistan falt kraftig etter grenselukkinger. Pakistan kunngjorde også planer om å åpne et konsulat i Benghazi, Libya, og marinen la frem en ny strategi som kombinerer mesh-nettverk med langdistanse-angrepskapasitet. 1,794 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
